explainedBy: The marketer and shopper stand together as the discussion pivots from evaluating people to judging commercial products.

storyboard.claim: The discussion shifts focus from judging individual human behavior to how we judge commerce.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer speaks in the office while the shopper listens attentively beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the discussion of brand flaws into consumer pricing psychology.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes both the commercial architect and everyday consumer on stage for the pricing chapter.

explainedBy: The shopper contemplates monetary value while holding a coin as the core metric of commerce.

storyboard.claim: We must examine how consumers evaluate the foundational metric of commerce: money and price.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper in the retail space looks down thoughtfully at a coin held in his hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from general commercial framing to the literal currency in the shopper's hand.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the abstract phrase 'core metric of commerce' in the physical coin being evaluated.

explainedBy: The shopper weighs subjective value against a price tag beside a balance scale.

storyboard.claim: Consumers have no intuitive compass for what a price tag genuinely signifies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper raises a hand in wonder beside a balance scale icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from holding the coin to evaluating the balance between price and perceived worth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the cognitive struggle of weighing worth with a balancing scale.

explainedBy: The shopper walks through the supermarket snack aisle tasked with buying party chips.

storyboard.claim: The scenario places the consumer in a supermarket snack aisle buying food for an office party.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper walks through the retail supermarket aisle looking at shelf selections.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the concrete grocery store scenario introduced by the host.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the consumer directly into the physical retail environment described in the scenario.

explainedBy: The shopper deliberates nervously between expensive premium chips and budget standard chips.

storyboard.claim: Premium chips cost double the standard brand, creating purchasing deliberation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper pauses in the aisle, pointing anxiously between different price points on the shelf.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the supermarket aisle sequence as the shopper encounters the price dilemma.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the steep 2x price disparity causing consumer anxiety.

explainedBy: The shopper discovers a middle-tier compromise brand positioned right between budget and premium.

storyboard.claim: A mid-tier option positioned between basic and luxury provides an appealing compromise.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper points toward the middle shelf with an expression of sudden discovery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Progresses from deliberation to discovering the middle compromise product on the shelf.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the exact spatial position in the middle that triggers the compromise heuristic.

explainedBy: The shopper celebrates with relief after choosing the middle-tier compromise option.

storyboard.claim: Selecting the compromise product relieves psychological decision friction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper celebrates with raised arms and a joyful smile in the aisle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the shelf tension as the purchase decision is happily executed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the earlier anxiety with emotional relief and self-satisfaction.

explainedBy: A spectrum diagram positions the purchase directly in the middle between budget and quality.

storyboard.claim: The consumer rationalizes the choice as a balanced compromise between cost and product quality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum diagram displaying a marker centered halfway between BUDGET and QUALITY.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Maps the shopper's internal self-justification into a formal decision scale.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reveals how the compromise effect creates the illusion of an exact mathematical midpoint.

explainedBy: The marketer smirks knowingly in the retail aisle, having engineered the shelf architecture.

storyboard.claim: Consumer valuation is manipulated by retail shelf architecture through anchoring.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer smirks and points at the shelves while the shopper stands slumped beside him in defeat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the consumer's rationalization to revealing the marketer's deliberate manipulation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the marketer's strategic control against the deceived shopper's deflation.

explainedBy: The shopper stares blankly at retail prices, facing the reality that absolute value does not exist.

storyboard.claim: Products have no inherent absolute pricing scale independent of context.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper looks on with a blank expression, unable to determine absolute price.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalizes the supermarket chip lesson into a universal psychological principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the consumer's cognitive numbness when stripped of objective price anchors.

explainedBy: The shopper stands with defeated posture as the idea of an internal price meter is struck through.

storyboard.claim: The human brain has no built-in objective valuation mechanism for goods.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper slumps in dismay while the words AN INTERNAL OBJECTIVE METER appear struck out in red.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly refutes the assumption that shoppers have internal price standards.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strikeout visually rejects the false assumption of an innate mental price gauge.

explainedBy: The marketer explains price relativity to the surprised shopper using the comparison set.

storyboard.claim: Valuation is entirely relative to the immediate reference frame presented to the buyer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer points out the comparison framework while the shopper touches his chin in realization.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the comparison set as the primary mechanism dictating perceived value.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates the marketer defining the perceptual boundary for the consumer.

explainedBy: The marketer introduces the Nespresso case study while holding a coffee cup.

storyboard.claim: The Nespresso coffee pod strategy provides the definitive case study in price anchoring.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer stands in a cafe set holding an espresso cup with a confident smile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from abstract price theory to the real-world Nespresso commercial example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the coffee cafe context immediately as the Nespresso case study begins.

explainedBy: The marketer points out the disastrous counterfactual: placing pods next to bulk supermarket coffee.

storyboard.claim: Positioning espresso pods next to standard bulk coffee bags would have destroyed the business.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer gestures warningly in the supermarket aisle beside a financial crash icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Constructs the disastrous alternative scenario where pods are framed against bulk coffee.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crash symbol underscores the fatal commercial risk of the wrong shelf placement.

explainedBy: The shopper recoils in anger at the shocking calculation of thirty-four pounds per pound of coffee.

storyboard.claim: Calculating the unit price reveals coffee pods cost an extortionate thirty-four pounds per pound.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper gestures in angry disbelief in the grocery aisle at the exorbitant price calculation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quantifies the mathematical reality behind why consumers would have rejected the pods.
storyboard.addedInformation: Converts the abstract price into the stark unit cost that would incite consumer outrage.

explainedBy: The marketer smiles strategically while shifting the comparison set away from bulk roast coffee.

storyboard.claim: Nestle circumvented price resistance by intentionally changing the consumer's comparison anchor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer in an agency setting talks with a knowing smirk, explaining the strategic reframing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the consumer's outrage to the marketer's framing masterstroke.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts consumer vulnerability against deliberate commercial design.

explainedBy: The consumer holds a cafe cup, anchoring value against a two-pound-fifty high-street barista drink.

storyboard.claim: Marketing single cups anchors the pod's cost against an expensive coffee shop drink.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper sits in a high-street cafe setting holding an espresso cup.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the new mental benchmark Nestle substituted for the supermarket bean aisle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the shopper directly in the cafe context that establishes the 2.50 mental price anchor.

explainedBy: The shopper happily looks at a coin, realizing thirty pence feels minuscule against a cafe anchor.

storyboard.claim: Compared to a multi-pound cafe drink, thirty pence feels remarkably cheap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper holds a small coin in the cafe with a pleasantly surprised smile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Compares the micro-cost of the pod directly against the expensive cafe benchmark.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the psychological relief when 30p is viewed alongside a 2.50 anchor.

explainedBy: The shopper celebrates feeling like he received an absolute massive bargain on coffee.

storyboard.claim: Shifting the comparison anchor rewired perceived value into a triumphant bargain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper celebrates enthusiastically in the cafe, convinced he scored a massive deal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the final consumer emotion resulting from Nestle's anchor manipulation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates the illusion of winning a bargain while paying premium margins.

explainedBy: The marketer presents Shotton's King Cobra beer experiment in a pub setting.

storyboard.claim: Richard Shotton empirically tested price anchoring using King Cobra premium beer in a pub.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer introduces the behavioral field test in a relaxed hospitality setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the corporate Nespresso case study to Shotton's own empirical field experiment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the specific venue used to test the anchoring mechanism.

explainedBy: The marketer points out the wine-shaped bottle placed beside standard small beer bottles.

storyboard.claim: The beer was packaged in a large corked bottle mimicking the physical form of wine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer gestures toward product displays, emphasizing the wine-bottle packaging format.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Highlights the key physical feature that allows the beer to bridge categories.
storyboard.addedInformation: Focuses attention on the packaging decoy that enables category cross-anchoring.

explainedBy: The shopper offers three pounds seventy-five when the beer is anchored against normal beers.

storyboard.claim: Anchored alongside regular beers, participants valued the bottle at three pounds seventy-five.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper in the tasting experiment names a modest price of 3.75.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the baseline valuation under the standard beer comparison set.
storyboard.addedInformation: Records the exact baseline price ceiling generated by ordinary beer anchors.

explainedBy: The marketer shifts the bottle into a lineup of expensive wines for the second tasting trial.

storyboard.claim: In the second trial, the identical beer was placed adjacent to premium wines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer points with an amused smirk to the newly arranged lineup of expensive wines.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Swaps the comparison anchor from ordinary beer to luxury wine bottles.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the experimental intervention where only the physical neighbor changes.

explainedBy: The shopper happily agrees to pay twenty-eight percent more for the exact same liquid.

storyboard.claim: Proximity to wine increased willingness to pay by twenty-eight percent for identical beer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper looks with wide eyes at the money in his hand, willing to pay significantly more.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the dramatic price inflation caused entirely by the wine adjacency.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the 28% premium generated purely by physical proximity to higher anchors.

explainedBy: The shopper challenges the marketer on whether anchoring effects persist over time.

storyboard.claim: The co-host questions whether consumers eventually see through visual anchoring tricks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper leans forward skeptically in conversation with the relaxed marketer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Injects skeptical counter-argument into the discussion of pricing tricks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the intellectual debate between consumer skepticism and behavioral permanence.

explainedBy: The shopper points to regulatory unit pricing as proof that consumers cannot be fooled.

storyboard.claim: Regulatory unit pricing provides standardized comparison metrics on supermarket shelves.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper points toward a shield icon representing consumer pricing regulations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Offers regulatory unit tags as the consumer's rational defense against framing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the shield icon to depict mandatory government price transparency as consumer protection.

explainedBy: The shopper studies a standardized price note, expecting rational math to prevail.

storyboard.claim: Consumers believe System 2 analytical thinking kicks in to calculate unit math.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper inspects a tiny pricing note closely, expecting deliberate logic to override framing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Details the cognitive process where consumers attempt conscious numerical calculation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the shopper relying on printed notes to calculate price per gram.

explainedBy: The shopper slumps in defeat as the marketer explains how brain architecture defeats rationality.

storyboard.claim: Human neural wiring actively resists rational mathematical correction against anchors.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper stands slumped in disappointment while the marketer calmly explains cognitive limits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shatters the hope that unit pricing protects consumers from subconscious bias.
storyboard.addedInformation: Physically contrasts the defeated consumer against the reality of cognitive architecture.

explainedBy: The marketer introduces Tversky and Kahneman's classic experiment on sticky anchors.

storyboard.claim: Tversky and Kahneman proved that arbitrary numbers cling to judgment even when known to be fake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer speaks beside an experiment notes icon, presenting academic evidence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions to the landmark psychological study demonstrating anchor persistence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Validates the host's claim with academic experimental provenance.

explainedBy: The shopper reaches out to spin a game wheel rigged to land on arbitrary numbers.

storyboard.claim: Participants spun a rigged wheel of fortune programmed to stop on 10 or 65.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper reaches out with a surprised look beside a game wheel icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Illustrates the experimental setup of the arbitrary casino wheel.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the artificial randomness of the initial anchor.

explainedBy: The marketer tasks the shopper with estimating a complex numerical fact right after the spin.

storyboard.claim: Researchers immediately asked subjects to estimate an unrelated global statistic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer questions the shopper, who points a finger to his chin in concentration.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the spin of the wheel to the estimation question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts the cognitive demand suddenly placed on the experimental subject.

explainedBy: The shopper ponders the percentage of African nations in the UN, noting the lack of connection.

storyboard.claim: The geopolitical estimation question possessed zero logical link to the wheel's numbers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper stands contemplating the complete irrelevance of the game to world geography.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Emphasizes the complete absurdity of connecting a wheel spin to UN member counts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Underlines the irrationality of the cognitive anchor being tested.

explainedBy: The shopper sees the wheel land on the low number ten as anchoring hijacks reasoning.

storyboard.claim: Anchoring hijacked reasoning when participants observed the wheel stop at ten.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper points in surprise at the low number 10 on the experimental display.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the low-anchor test condition in Kahneman's experiment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Isolates the single arbitrary number 10 that primes the first experimental group.

explainedBy: The shopper records the low guess of twenty-five percent before the wheel shifts to sixty-five.

storyboard.claim: Subjects anchored to the number 10 estimated an average of twenty-five percent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper reports the suppressed twenty-five percent guess produced by the low anchor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the quantitative output of the low-anchor condition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Records the exact statistical distortion caused by the random number 10.

explainedBy: The shopper reacts with shock at the massive jump to forty-five percent under the high anchor.

storyboard.claim: The group anchored to sixty-five guessed forty-five percent, revealing deep cognitive distortion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper gestures with open-mouthed astonishment at the massive discrepancy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Compares the high-anchor result against the twenty-five percent low-anchor baseline.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the wild 20-percentage-point distortion produced by pure randomness.

explainedBy: The shopper reaches toward a target icon but stops short, showing incomplete adjustment.

storyboard.claim: Humans anchor to initial values and make systematically insufficient logical adjustments.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper reaches toward a target icon but stops short, showing incomplete adjustment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the psychological mechanism behind why anchors remain sticky.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the failure to adjust sufficiently away from an arbitrary starting point.

explainedBy: The marketer points out high price decoys and packaging that irreversibly trap the consumer.

storyboard.claim: Product packaging, shelf location, and expensive decoys irreversibly lock in price perception.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer smirks while pointing at shelf decoys as the shopper stands dejectedly beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows how commercial marketers exploit insufficient adjustment on retail shelves.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the commercial decoys specifically engineered to inflate baseline valuations.

explainedBy: The shopper stares with blank disillusionment as price logic is revealed as an illusion.

storyboard.claim: Rational price calculation based on economic utility is a cognitive illusion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper slumps with a blank expression, confronting the unreality of price logic.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the chapter's core finding on the fictional nature of absolute value.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the collapse of traditional neoclassical utility theory.

explainedBy: The marketer stands before the retail environment he designed to trigger heuristic shortcuts.

storyboard.claim: Purchases are predictable heuristic shortcuts steered by environmental context and framing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer gestures confidently in the retail store beside a lightbulb insight icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the chapter on anchoring with the marketer's strategic perspective.
storyboard.addedInformation: Celebrates the behavioral science power of choice architecture.

explainedBy: The shopper holds a wallet, transitioning to how the physical act of paying influences spending.

storyboard.claim: Willingness to spend depends heavily on the physical mechanics of the transaction itself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper on a city street holds a leather wallet in his hands thoughtfully.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from price anchoring to the physical friction of payment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the wallet prop to embody the physical vehicle of payment.

explainedBy: The shopper holds out cash, representing the tactile friction of handing over money.

storyboard.claim: Behavioral economics proves tactile payment friction restrains spending far more than price.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper looks down anxiously at a coin held in his palm on the city street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dramatizes the physical pain of parting with physical currency.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes tactile friction literal through the hesitant physical holding of cash.

explainedBy: The shopper walks into an artisan cafe during a mid-morning slump to order coffee.

storyboard.claim: Fatigued consumers visit local cafes seeking relief through routine coffee purchases.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The weary shopper walks into a warm artisan cafe seeking caffeine during a work slump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the narrative scene for the contactless payment temptation story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the emotional fatigue driving the consumer's impulse cafe visit.

explainedBy: The shopper holds a smartphone ready to tap payment at the counter while spotting pastry.

storyboard.claim: Frictionless digital payment removes spending hesitation right as visual temptations appear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shopper holds his smartphone toward the payment reader while his eyes widen at pastries.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Freezes the moment of decision right before frictionless contactless payment occurs.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the held smartphone as the friction-free payment tool enabling impulse spending.
